It happened on a random day in October. Mydei still remembered that the weather that day was unusually warm – the wind was refreshing instead of bitingly cold, the birds were softly chirping and the trees were still clad in their golden glory, not yet naked to the human eye.

The day was perfect. It was warm, sunny – the ideal time to go out and spend time with your friends and loved ones, to enjoy your time together.

It was on a day like this that Mydei’s heart was irrevocably broken.

*

Mydei wondered what was the point of no return.

How had he never noticed it.

It didn’t start with a big fight. Now that he looked back, he realized the warning signs have always been there – flashing red, trying, begging to be noticed. Impossible to miss, really.

Too bad Mydei was so busy being in love that all the warning signs went straight over his head.

The day that started this spiral began just like any other – Mydei woke up to an empty bed and with a bright sticky note on the bedside table.

“Went to work :( Already fed the beast. Don’t wait up for me!”

He smiled, carefully folding the note. He knew how much Phainon has been working, how busy their law firm has been for the past few months, trying so hard to secure the deal with Penacony. He didn’t think much of it before sending a text to his boyfriend.

“Going on a walk with Castorice. The dinner will be in the fridge.

Good luck. Love you.”

He hadn’t even put down the phone when he already got multiple responses from Phainon, as if he’d been waiting for him to wake up.

He stood up from their bed and stretched for a bit – all this workload at the bakery has been making him rusty; he really needed to find some time to hit up the gym. Perhaps he will even drag Phainon there once he was done with his current project at work.

Making his way to their kitchen, he quickly prepared breakfast. Sitting alone at the dining table, he absentmindedly stared out the window. The window in their kitchen was slightly open, making his hair flutter in the air – he carelessly tied it up, and took a bite of his food.

The savory breakfast burst with flavor in his mouth, making him let out an unconscious hum as he indulged himself with a smile.

It really was a good day. If only Phainon wasn’t called out to work it would have been absolutely perfect.

He quietly washed the dishes when something soft and furry brushed against his bare legs. He heard an indignant meow coming from somewhere below and looked down with a raised eyebrow.

“Hello. I’ve been told you’ve been already fed.” He bent down a little to pet the big orange cat. Nikador has been a fairly new addition to their house – he used to be a street cat, one that loved to spend his time around Mydei’s bakery. Apparently, that was his ‘territory’ before Mydei dared to encroach on it.

The bakery was supposed to be a somewhat side-business for Mydei, a little hobby, or a pet project, as some called it. As a beloved heir to a multibillion company Kremnos, Mydei had no reason to work a day in his life. His parents were still young and knew Mydei didn’t want to take any part in the family business. Eurypon and Gorgo, though strict, loved him a lot – they let him do whatever he wanted and supported him in everything. Their only requirement was for him to know the basics, so if it was ever needed, he could take control of the company and have his finger on its pulse. Mydei easily agreed. He finished business school, got a degree, made a deal with Krateros and his friends that worked at the company that they would regularly give him updates on the family business and only then he opened his bakery – his little place of haven.

It wasn’t a big place – it was strategically placed in the little alley in the middle of the city, hidden unless you looked for it. The first time he saw it he instantly fell in love. He could’ve already imagined how he would decorate it, where he’d put the tables, what kind of music he’d play and what kind of menu he’d prepare that would be worthy of this place. It was love at first sight.

Mydei fought tooth and nail for that place, went through one struggle after another – the place had incredible charm but it was old and, as it always happened with old places, it came with its own set of problems. Electricity, heating, constant flooding and never-ending renovations – it took a few years before Mydei officially opened his bakery.

But it happened on his terms, with his close friends and family behind him. It was the happiest day in his life.

And this was also the place where he met Phainon again. He was one of the first customers that visited his bakery, one that became a regular as soon as he tasted Mydei’s special golden honeycakes. It was too, love at first sight for him.

Or love at first taste, Mydei thought with amusement.

A slightly shrill meow pulled him from his memories. Mydei blinked and lightly flicked Nikador’s fluffy head.

“No more food for you. Look at how big you’ve become. If it continues this way I’ll have to buy a leash and bring you on my morning runs,” he threatened. Nikador bristled as soon as he heard the cursed phrase – ‘morning runs’. Mydei only saw an orange flash before the cat disappeared around the corner. For such a lazy creature he sure ran fast when needed.

The king of the streets. More like a lazy, always hungry menace.

He grabbed his phone and shot a quick text to Castorice, letting her know that he’ll be at their place in 20 minutes. Seeing her response, he put his phone down and got ready. There was something he wanted to grab from his bakery, so he had to hurry.

*

By the time Mydei and Castorice met up the park was unsurprisingly full of people. The summer sun and its blistering heat had finally faded into the autumn afternoons, washing the people basking in sunlight with its gentle warmth. It took some time before they found a quiet corner right under a big tree, shaded from everyone’s prying eyes.

Mydei and Castorice met through Phainon, during one of the corporate events they had at the law firm. Something involving team-building, if Mydei remembered correctly. It was the first time Phainon had officially took him as his plus one, introducing him to everyone as his boyfriend. Mydei remembered how worried he was before the event – he never cared what others thought of him but still, he wanted to make a good impression as Phainon’s partner. He knew Phainon had also never taken anyone as his date to any event, always preferring to go alone and brush off everyone’s questions about when he was going to bring someone to show off. It was the first time for both of them and Mydei wanted it to be perfect.

The introduction went without a hitch – surprisingly, the boss Phainon had talked so much about was a dear friend of Mydei’s mother, one that knew him since he was very young.

“So, you are the man that has our dear Phainon wrapped around his finger,” she laughed when she finally saw him, her gold eyes sparkling with humor.

A blush brightened his features. No matter how much he tried he couldn’t hide the warmth that flooded his cheeks. Still, he returned her embrace with a smile.

“It’s been a long time. it’s nice to see you again, Aglaea.”

It was on that event where he met Castorice, a plus one of Phainon’s colleague, Cipher. She was standing on the balcony, breathing in the fresh air and enjoying the soft night when Mydei joined her in her solitude. The night was beautiful and with quiet smiles an unlikely friendship had sparked.

It’s been a long time since then – in the meantime Castorice had married her long-term girlfriend Cipher and Mydei had finally moved in with Phainon, their relationship growing stronger by the day.

Breathing in the scent of fresh leaves, Mydei leaned on the tree behind him with a sigh. He passed the bundle of freshly baked cookies to Castorice – he was trying a new recipe and had some leftovers. He thought she’d like the savory taste this batch had thanks to the miso paste he added on Phainon’s suggestion. He tried one before giving them to her, they were pretty good. Sprinkled with some flaky salt and they were ready to be served to their customers. Perhaps he would add them to their menu later.

And based on Castorice’s happy little dance she liked them well enough.

“Thank you,” she popped another cookie into her mouth. “Delicious as always.”

The sun softly caressed their faces, as if giving them a gentle kiss. Mydei smiled at his friend and quickly shot a picture of their picnic blanket for Phainon. He knew his boyfriend was probably dying under assignments, so he made sure to attach a picture of leftover cookies with a note.

“There are some for you at home. It’s the ones with miso; you seemed to like them. Come home sooner.”

His lips quirked up at Phainon’s immediate response. No matter the constant cold war between Nikador and Phainon, they were truly too similar in some aspects. He quickly pocketed his phone and raised his head, accidentally meeting Castroice’s eyes.

“Phainon,” he explained, waving his hand carelessly. “He’s stuck in the office, working on their big project. I’m sure you know – I think Cipher is involved too.”

The sun had slowly dipped behind the clouds, taking with it the warmth that kissed their faces just a moment ago. Mydei swiftly took a fluffy blanket from his bag and covered himself and Castorice with it. The weather was unpredictable; he didn’t want any of them to get sick.

Hearing no response, Mydei looked at her and noticed her curious if slightly confused smile.

He didn’t know at the time that the next words she said would destroy the illusion that was his happy relationship.

(It started here.)

“The one with Penacony?” seeing his nod, she tucked a strand of lavender hair behind her ear before continuing without a thought. “But didn’t they finish it almost a month ago? I think Cipher even took some days off to emotionally recover after they were finally done.”

She smiled at him as if they were sharing an inner joke. And of course, why wouldn’t she think that – she’s been with Cipher for so long, she more than anyone in Mydei’s life knew what it was like being married to a successful lawyer. Late nights and constant business trips were the least of their worries.

Too bad that this time Mydei had no idea what she was talking about.

He shook his head with a frown. “No, they didn’t. Phainon has been stuck in the office all this time because he was working on it. He would have told me if they were done.”

And he would have, Mydei knows that – they met when Phainon was just starting to work at the company, Mydei was there with him from the very beginning of his journey, celebrating all his wins like they were his own. And with this project in particular – Mydei had sat with Phainon until three in the morning, helping him with the documents, listening and correcting his speech, so that everyone would be satisfied with his delivery. He saw how stressed Phainon was and tried to help as much as he could – there was no way Phainon wouldn’t have told him that the deal went through. It just wasn’t possible.

Castorice fidgeted a little with her phone, scrolling for a bit, before turning the screen to him and showing him a picture of her and Cipher in their apartment.

Mydei visited them a few times, he recognized their home immediately. The Cipher in the photo was buried in Castorice embrace, one tired cyan eye peeking from under her arm. She was clearly relaxing at home when her wife took the picture – the bags under her eyes and the dark red shirt she stole from Mydei during one of their trips was a dead giveaway.

“That was taken the next day after they finally closed the deal.” Castorice shuffled to his side, so that she also could look at the photo. She smiled softly, “She doesn’t like to admit it, but Cipher really needed some peace and quiet after it. It took a lot from her, both physically and emotionally.” She swiped to show another picture, this time with Cipher sleeping under a blanket with their cat in her arms. “I thought she’d want go out to celebrate the closing of the deal but she was so dead on her feet, that we stayed home the whole weekend.”

Mydei looked at the date of the photo – a month ago. The photos were taken a month ago, just as Castorice said.

He knew there was no reason for her to lie. Yet he couldn’t understand for what reason Phainon would lie to him.

Mydei tried to remember what they did on the day the deal was supposedly done. It’s been some time ago but he still remembered that was one of the rare days Phainon had come home early.

He remembered it was a regular day at the bakery. Nothing memorable happened that day and he left the keys to Hyacine, trusting her to get everything in order and close on time. He had some documents to take care of at home – Hephaestion texted him that morning, telling him the monthly report was sent today and he should look at it when he had the chance, the team wanted to know his opinion on some topics mentioned there.

He came home, fed Nikador and took a shower – his usual routine. After preparing himself some food he quickly looked through reports Hephaestion mentioned. It was around that time that Phainon sent him a text, telling him that Aglaea let them off early today, so he’ll be home soon.

They clearly had different interpretations of what ‘soon’ meant because in the time it took Phainon to get to their apartment, Mydei prepared dinner, cleaned the apartment and even took a small nap. It was during that brief moment of rest that he heard the door open. Nikador grumbled somewhere around his neck before he stood up and went to greet his ‘father’. Mydei was usually a very heavy sleeper but since Phainon had texted him earlier he wanted to wait for him – it’s been so long since they properly spent time together, he didn’t want to miss even a second of it.

Mydei felt the bed dip and groggily opened his eyes. “Hey,” he smiled softly, reaching a hand towards him. “Welcome home.”

Phainon, eyes bright, took his hand and gently kissed the back of it. “It’s good to be home. Did I wake you?”

“No, it’s fine,” he murmured before trying to sit up. “How was your day?” He gave Phainon a light pat on his cheek and then rubbed his eyes with a yawn.

“It was,” Phainon stood up and took off his jacket. He slightly stumbled over his words. “Good. We made big progress today.”

Mydei raised his head. “Oh? A celebration is in order?”

Phainon laughed. He was wearing his favorite dark blue suit today, the one that made a striking contrast with his light hair and made his brilliant blue eyes shine even more. He lost his dark tie somewhere and the first three buttons of his shirt were already unbuttoned, showing a glimpse of his well-defined chest. Slightly more awake now, Mydei raised an eyebrow at his state.

“What happened?”

Phainon waved off his questions. “it’s nothing, don’t worry about it. Now about that celebration…” He shrugged off his shirt and grabbed Mydei’s legs, dragging him to the edge of the bed. Slotting himself between his thighs, Phainon firmly pressed his hand on Mydei’s neck forcing him to raise his head. Caged in like this, Mydei could only stare wide-eyed at his boyfriend, fully awake this time.

Phainon caressed his face with his other hand and smiled down at him. “I have some ideas in mind.”

There was not much talking done after that.

“Mydei?” Castorice worried voice drew him back from his memories. He looked at her with a start. “Hasn’t Phainon… mentioned anything?”

He shook his head.

No, he hasn’t. And now that Mydei thought about it, Phainon hasn’t mentioned any actual details about the deal in some time. Even when Mydei asked, he hadn’t said anything, instead trying to divert his attention to something else.

A month. He hasn’t mentioned anything in a month, a disoriented voice in the back of his head whispered. But why?

Castorice seemed a little taken aback. After all, she also knew Phainon. She knew how unusual this was.

The wind picked up, tugging at their clothes. The sun was still hiding behind the clouds.

She glanced down at the phone loosely held in Mydei’s hand, and gently touched his shoulder.

“Maybe, I’m wrong. Perhaps there was some additional details that needed Phainon’s attention or,” she said encouragingly, “maybe I really am talking about a different project. You know how it is – they have such massive workload, it’s impossible to keep up.”

She really was too good to him, Mydei smiled, golden eyes staring fixatedly at their picnic blanket. But it was too late now – the floodgates have already been opened. The first seed of doubt has been planted.

Observant as always, Castorice noticed his muddled state, her delicate eyebrows furrowing a bit. “I’m sorry for making you uncomfortable.” She said, her voice uncharacteristically quiet. Purple eyes shone in guilt, as if it was her fault that Mydei’s boyfriend has been possibly lying to him for weeks.

Mydei’s mind was a blur of images, trying and failing to make sense of anything. The late nights, the constant excuses… Even today Phainon had used the Penacony deal to get out of spending their morning together. Surely, there must be a reason?

“No,” he forced another smile to his face. It’s not Castorice’s fault, he repeated. There has to be a reason. “I will talk to him. Thank you for telling me,” the smile Mydei sent her this time was small but genuine. “You’re a good friend, Castorice.”

The sun has finally peeked out from the clouds, flooding him with warmth he couldn’t feel.

*

They had to part ways soon after that conversation – Cipher was waiting for Castorice at home and Mydei… There was only an empty apartment to welcome him. And his fat cat Nikador, of course.

When Mydei finally closed the door to his and Phainon’s apartment, Castorice’s last words still lingered in his head.

Her light touch stopped him in his tracks. Mydei turned to look at her, immediately meeting her sad smile.

“I feel like this is somehow my fault,” seeing him open his mouth ready to refute her, she quickly shook her head. “No, please, listen to me. I’ve known Phainon for more than five years. This has to be some kind of misunderstanding.”

“Please. Talk to him before making up your mind.”

He appreciated the reminder but there was no need for it – he planned on talking first anyway. He didn’t like doubting his boyfriend, in all years they’ve been together Phainon has never given him a reason to do so. He was the perfect partner, the most considerate and loving man he’s ever known.

Once he’s gotten out of his head, he realized how unreasonably he’s been acting. That must have been what prompted Castorice to tell him not to jump to any conclusions.

Mydei roughly ran his hand through his hair. Phainon was the love of his life. Of course, he was going to talk to him first.

He nimbly sidestepped Nikador’s attack of the day and made his way to the kitchen. That reminded him – the beast was out for blood. It was time to feed it.

Everything else could wait.

*

Mydei really tried to wait for Phainon to come home so that they could have a talk. He didn’t want to wait – he felt like the longer he waited, the worse it could become. He was always the kind of person that went straight to the root of the problem, trying to solve it as quickly as possible. He was never one to dawdle. But… the bed was right there. And he was dead on his feet.

He didn’t hear when Phainon came in. His first clue that something might have changed from the usual routine of the past month was a familiar naked chest pressing against his back.

Slightly more awake now, he felt strong arms circle his waist, drawing him closer and closer until there was no space between their bodies.

“Shhh, go to sleep. I’ve got you,” Phainon whispered, placing a hot kiss on the side of his neck.

Half asleep, Mydei turned his head but before he could even open his mouth, Phainon was quick to claim his lips in a deep kiss. Tasting the slightly bitter taste of alcohol on Phainon’s tongue, Mydei furrowed his brows but still unconsciously relaxed in his hold, becoming boneless in less than a second. He felt Phainon’s hand take its usual place – under his shirt, softly fondling his chest, rolling one perked nipple between his fingers – and he couldn’t help but relax even further.

He was asleep before he knew it, not even feeling the kiss Phainon left on his nape.

The next day Mydei once again woke up to an empty bed, but this time Phainon’s side wasn’t ice cold – instead it was slightly warm, still retaining some of the heat from his body. Hearing a mocking tune coming from the kitchen, he knew Phainon was home – his boyfriend only ever sang that song when he was making fun of their cat.

An angry hiss coming a second later only confirmed his thoughts. Mydei smiled into his pillow before turning his head and looking at Phainon’s side of the bed. Seeing rumpled sheets, he quickly looked around and shuffled slightly before laying his head on his boyfriend’s pillow. Breathing in deep, he felt satisfaction curl in his chest – Phainon was still wearing the cologne he bought him a few years ago.

As Mydei buried deeper into Phainon’s pillow, he could feel his chest tighten from affection, his cheeks hurting from how hard he was smiling.

Phainon is home.

The effect he had on Mydei was truly embarrassing sometimes.

The second he let his thoughts wander he heard the door of the bedroom open. Phainon stuck his head inside and seeing him awake, he beamed at him with his signature radiant smile.

“You’re up!” Mydei noticed that he was wearing Mydei’s own pink apron, the one Cipher got him in exchange for the red shirt she stole. He remembered how hard she laughed when she saw him actually wear it but the apron was useful and Mydei has never been one to waste clothes, so the apron stayed. Cipher eventually realized that he actually quite liked the, admittedly, very ugly thing and bought him more things from the set. Mydei really should have expected that Phainon, notoriously known for his bad taste, would also grow fond of it.

“Wait here, don’t get up!” Phainon quickly ran to the kitchen and came back with a tray filled to the brim with Mydei’s favorite breakfast food – there was a plate of honeycakes topped with syrup and fresh pomegranate seeds, Phainon’s signature light salad, some fresh fruit tarts from Mydei’s own bakery and even a variety of drinks.

Mydei looked at everything and couldn’t help but raise his eyebrows in surprise. “What’s all this for? What’s the occasion?”

Phainon cut a piece of the homemade golden honeycakes and offered it to Mydei. Only when Mydei opened his mouth, he responded with a smile, “Do I need a special occasion to spoil you?”

Still chewing, Mydei shot him a skeptical look.

It wasn’t that unusual for Phainon to make breakfast in bed. For Phainon from a month ago, that is. Current Phainon was always so busy with work – it was considered a good day if Mydei managed to catch a glimpse of him these days, nevermind breakfast in bed.

That actually reminded him of the conversation he had with Castorice yesterday.

Mydei took a second to look at his boyfriend. He looked just as usual – all happy smiles and bright eyes. Even the ugly pink apron didn’t ruin his look, instead adding a special charm only Phainon could pull off.

He looked like Phainon. The Phainon Mydei fell in love with years ago. The one he wanted to spend the rest of his life with.

Not wanting to beat around the bush, Mydei changed the topic, “I met Castorice yesterday.”

“Yeah? How is she, by the way?”

Mydei took another bite of the offered honeycakes. “Fine. She and Cipher bought a new car. The model is pretty good, especially for those with kids.”

He saw Phainon mouth drop in awe. “Kids? They’re planning for kids?”

“They are,” Mydei smiled imagining the picture-perfect couple. That image, more than anything, prompted him to finally say what’s been bothering him since last night. He needed to know.

Mydei tried to be casual about it at first. “Castorice also mentioned that the Penacony deal went through. That the deal has been done for more than a month, in fact. Is that true?”

He saw Phainon freeze.

“Phainon?” Calm down.

Phainon jerked his head and laughed sheepishly. “I must have forgotten to tell you. Yes, the deal went through, we got everything finalized a few weeks ago. It’s not yet put into practice but the groundwork is already there and that’s what matters, if you ask me.”

Something inside of Mydei wilted.

That was a lie. His smile always twitches at the corners when he lies. Mydei knows him better than anyone.

Phainon is lying to him.

Mydei quickly pushed the feeling down. He still needed answers because that was not the thing that made him worried. It was fine if Phainon forgot to tell him about the successful closing of the most important deal in his career, really, Mydei knew how much he worked and how many cases he had to deal with daily – it was a given that something might fall through or get forgotten in the process.

No, that was the least of his worries. If Phainon had really forgot to tell him then Mydei would have just thrown a late celebration for him at home and stopped thinking about the whole thing. He wasn’t unreasonable after all.

It was more so the fact that Phainon still used that deal to get out of spending his time with Mydei. Even yesterday, the Penacony deal was his excuse.

Mydei remembered the many texts telling him how Phainon was going to be late, that Aglaea had asked them to stay in the office, that someone on their team sent the wrong draft to the clients and now Phainon had to stay and work overtime to fix everything… It was one thing after another. At first Mydei remembered being worried because even at the peak of it the Penacony team hadn’t caused so many problems but when he brought his concerns to Phainon he was quick to reassure him.

“It’s okay. It should pass soon enough.”

“Don’t worry, they’re just trying to squeeze as much from us as possible. Since we’re not giving in, we’re kind of stuck in this headlock for now.”

“This is normal. Expected, really.”

After hearing the same thing over and over again, Mydei stopped asking and took Phainon at his word – why wouldn’t he? Phainon has never lied to him. At least, not when it came to this. That was before he talked to Castorice.

Now Mydei wasn’t so sure.

Still, he tried again. “Just yesterday, you said…”

Suddenly Phainon interrupted him, slightly jolting forward as if he expected Mydei to bring this up. “Oh,” his expression was sweet, a little sheepish as he rubbed the back of his head. “That’s a different contract, my dear Mydeimos. Since our original deal was so successful, Penacony decided they wanted us on more of their projects.”

He’s still going with it? “Really.”

“What, you don’t believe me? Ask anyone, they’d tell you the same thing!”

He tried to act natural, as if he was unbothered and maybe, if Mydei didn’t know him so well, he would’ve believed him. Unfortunately for Phainon, Mydei knew him. Perhaps even too well.

What he had trouble detecting before became crystal clear now.

“Phainon. Are you sure there isn’t anything you want to tell me?” Last chance.

“Yeah. Why?” Big blue eyes blinked at him in confusion.

Breathe out. “No reason. Thank you for the breakfast. It was delicious.”

Anyone, huh? Alright.

Seeing as Phainon was adamant on continuing the lie, it appeared that Mydei had to try another angle.

As soon as Phainon left the room taking the tray of food with him, Mydei unplugged his phone from the charger and opened his chat with Cipher. She may be Phainon’s colleague but he was much closer to her. Their friendship came first.

There was no need for empty pleasantries between them.

I’m fine, thank you for asking!

I’m the point of contact for everything related to Penacony. They can’t do anything without going through me first

There are no more deals. At least, not ones related to Penacony.

Mydei slowly turned off his phone. There, he had it now.

Undeniable proof that Phainon was hiding something from him.
